correspondence.finding: The initial selected opening occupies the northern part of an irregular unnamed lake complex. The original depicts its eastward transfer into the adjoining lake and narrow connecting waters, followed by the southeastward lake arm and the eastward continuation. The separate larger southwestern lake and nearby parallel pond chains are not substituted for the chosen route. No headwater name or definitive natural source point is established.

The source shows the selected eastward succession of small waters and channels, its southward loop, and the approach into the southern end of the longer north-oriented lake. The connecting stream and nearby southern and eastern lake arrivals are visible. Thematic letters, elevation figures and wildlife boundaries do not provide river names or substitute for these hydrographic joins.

The north-oriented lake, its narrow northern outlet, intervening channel and west-side approach into the larger Zeta Lake waterbody are continuously depicted. Side lakes and the distinct eastern stream arrivals remain separate from the selected western approach. No individual name is established for the southern approach lake or its connecting river.

Zeta Lake is explicitly labeled on the Washburn Lake original and again immediately north of the shared boundary on the Cape Stang original. The selected northward passage follows the connected lake waterbody, including its irregular shores, islands, narrows and cross-sheet continuation. The name is supported for this lake component; no exact northern name-boundary vertex or uniform name for every connected basin is assigned.

The northern broad lake passage, its neck to the southern waterbody, the long eastern arm and the outlet succession of narrow channels and elongated waters are visible on the original. The gray management boundary crosses the lake but is distinguishable from its shore and open-water continuation. The source does not establish a separate name for the northern lake passage or an exact extent of the Zeta Lake label.

The source traces the selected eastward river below the lake outlet, including its parallel channels around narrow islands, intervening widened waters and northern and southern stream arrivals. It then turns southeast toward the lower southern bend. The wildlife-management caption over part of the corridor does not prevent ordinary-scale reading of the connected river. No river hydronym is printed along this inspected interval.

The lower river descends south, receives the western lake outlet and other side streams, then bends east and northeast. The original shows the chosen through-channel and material junctions throughout this bend, distinct from the adjacent lake chain and the separate northern tributary. No exact modern channel alignment or branch-name boundary is claimed.

The final eastward river and its receiving shoreline are visible on the original. The channel enters the western shore of the water explicitly labeled Norway Bay, south of a separate northern coastal stream. The source supports the selected terminal at ordinary coastal-corridor scale; the map label names the receiving bay, not the river, and no precise present shoreline or tidal limit is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Arizona opening between the Bates Mountains and Cipriano Hills
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and first west-northwest approach lie in the foothill/plain setting between the Bates Mountains and Cipriano Hills. The source exposes the terrain, Pozo Nuevo Road and adjacent drainages, but does not establish the entire chosen opening as a connected named waterway leading into San Cristobal Wash. No neighboring wash name is transferred to this approach.

correspondence.component_scope: San Cristobal Wash near the plain north and northeast of Sheep Mountain
correspondence.finding: The original directly labels the dashed watercourse San Cristobal Wash north and northeast of Sheep Mountain, across the Bates Well Road corridor. A portion of the selected northwest-going course follows that named wash at ordinary corridor scale. This supports the natural reach name, without assigning exact name-transition vertices or making the name cover the earlier foothill approach or the later westward plain crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward plain departure, small waterbody setting and southbound O’Neill Hills passage
correspondence.finding: The selected course leaves the mapped San Cristobal Wash corridor westward across the plain south of the Antelope Hills, turns south near small mapped waterbody footprints, and continues west of the O’Neill Hills. The original does not establish the selected transfer from San Cristobal Wash, connected passages through those small waterbodies, or the full southbound through-link toward the international boundary. The small features are not promoted to named lakes or verified lake connectors.

correspondence.component_scope: International-border passage, Highway 2 crossing and Volcán Colorado setting
correspondence.finding: The selected southbound route crosses the international-boundary setting, Mexico Highway 2 and the area east of Volcán Romo and beside Volcán Colorado, then approaches the east side of Volcán El Elegante. The state original shows separate intermittent drainage approaches and volcanic terrain. It supplies regional correspondence for the whole interval but does not demonstrate every selected through-link from the Arizona plain into the southbound Mexican drainage. No El Tapón or La Tinaja name is assigned from the separate western Pinacate drainages.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Pinacate corridor from El Elegante and Cerro San Pedro to Sierra Blanca
correspondence.finding: The selection runs down the eastern Pinacate/Ladrilleros margin, past the Cerro San Pedro setting and toward Sierra Blanca. Both Mexican originals depict unnamed drainage lines and tributary joins in this corridor. The municipal relief map gives the connected local drainage setting at finer regional scale, but it does not name the selected reach or settle the preceding northward connection. The separately labeled Palo Fierro and Sonoyta courses are not extended over this western selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward lower turn across the dune/plain setting and actual Gulf coast ending
correspondence.finding: South of Sierra Blanca the selection turns west across the dune/plain setting toward the Gulf of California coast northwest of Puerto Peñasco, north of the Bahía la Choya setting on the state sheet. The municipal map depicts a dune field and neighboring drainage continuing south toward the coast east of Punta Peñasco, but does not show the selected westward through-connection to the actual ending. The endpoint is not relocated to the named Sonoyta line, Playa Encanto, Punta Peñasco or another obvious mapped drainage mouth. The coastal setting is established; a selected continuous river outlet is not.

The western opening and initial eastward lake-country route lie in the southern Peters study setting. RG99-07 Figure2 does not portray the chosen small stream network or identify the source waterbody. CEHQ is not sufficiently legible and detailed here. No headwater name or connection is established.

The selected short northward excursion and return toward the southeast require primary correspondence for the actual intervening waterways and joins. Neither inspected map shows that chosen connected course in sufficient detail. A nearby regional lake name is not assigned to this passage.

The selected southeastward path crosses the southern part of the Peters study area. Figure2 simplifies away the river network and does not support successive lake inlets, outlets or tributary connections. CEHQ supplies only regional neighboring-drainage context.

The chosen southern dip is partly south of RG99-07 Figure2’s geographic extent. CEHQ’s generalized regional drainage does not establish the actual lake/stream passage and eastward turn. The chosen route has not been replaced by an adjacent clearer river.

No inspected original establishes the actual northeastward lower connections and waterbody transitions. The selected route approaches and then passes east of the Peters figure extent; regional names and discovery text are insufficient to demonstrate these joins.

The actual eastern terminal approach lies outside RG99-07 Figure2’s eastern extent and is not established by the CEHQ view. Rivière au Chien Rouge appears as a discovery lead for this vicinity, but no readable permitted primary terminal map or original route prose was inspected to establish that assignment. No exact mouth, current tidal limit or full-group identity is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected northern opening and upper approach
correspondence.finding: The opening corresponds to the mapped Río Blanco branch, followed through its visible upper junction into the south-running trunk and southeastward valley course. The upper network, opening and continuation are visible rather than inferred solely from basin membership.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: The map does not label every intervening reach. The name Río Chirripó Pacífico and its exact transition are not accepted here from discovery snippets or an unread source. Río Blanco is retained only for the clearly labelled upper branch.

correspondence.finding: The full middle fragment follows the continuous mapped trunk through the General valley to the lower Coto Brus joining area. Río General is visibly labelled on this inland trunk; the connected side streams and change in direction provide corridor context.
The entire selected eastern approach corresponds to the labelled lower Río Coto Brus, continuing westward to the separately retained short tributary fragment. It is not relabelled General or Térraba.

This separately assessed short fragment is the downstream continuation of the selected Coto Brus approach into its confluence with the General trunk. The source shows the joining channel rather than only two nearby name labels.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Térraba and selected estuarine continuation
correspondence.finding: The western lower trunk corresponds to Río Térraba and continues through Palmar Norte and Ciudad Cortés into the northern estuarine network. The selected trace approaches Isla Viuda and turns into the channel network toward the Boca Nueva–Boca Brava sector. The actual selected endpoint is within that estuarine network; it is not claimed to be Boca Coronado or a surveyed ocean-mouth point.
correspondence.name_scope_limit: The representative river name does not establish the exact local estero name or an ocean-outlet name for the final stored point.

joins_and_connectors.component: Upper Río Blanco branch to inland trunk
joins_and_connectors.status: Visible connected network at the source scale; exact intervening name transition not asserted.

joins_and_connectors.component: Boundary between selected mainstem fragments 10737 and 10738
joins_and_connectors.status: Continuous mapped inland valley corridor; no artificial connector inferred.

joins_and_connectors.component: Tributary 10740 to tributary 10741, then General–Coto Brus junction and lower mainstem 10739
joins_and_connectors.status: Both tributary fragments independently accounted for and continuous joining sequence visible.

joins_and_connectors.component: Lower river into northern Térraba-Sierpe estuary and actual terminal
joins_and_connectors.status: Original Figure 1 shows the lower river, Isla Viuda and branching estuarine channels; the selected endpoint is assessed within this mapped network, not substituted by the article’s separate Boca Coronado longitudinal profile.

No lake/reservoir crossing or required managed connector is depicted along the selected corridor in these historical sources. The El Diquís project discussed hypothetically in the 2015 article is not treated as an existing selected impoundment or evidence of present operation.
